papers.title: H13–partially stabilized zirconia nanocomposites fabricated by high-energy mechanical milling and selective laser melting
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Industrial Engineering, University of Trento, Trento, Italy

corresponding_authors.name: Bandar AlMangour
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA 02138, USA

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关于工具钢与氧化锆纳米复合材料的制备，与生物医学植入物和多孔骨盆力学无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on H13 tool steel and zirconia nanocomposites for wear-resistant applications, with no biomedical context, no porous implant structures, no stress shielding analysis, and no osseointegration evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 制备具有高耐磨性的H13钢与氧化锆纳米复合材料。
summary_zh.method: 通过高能机械研磨和选区激光熔化制备复合材料。
summary_zh.result: 复合材料显微硬度提高，耐磨性优于纯H13钢。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微硬度测试和磨损实验验证性能。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate H13 steel and partially stabilized zirconia nanocomposites with enhanced wear resistance for tooling applications.
summary_en.method: High-energy mechanical milling was used to mix powders, followed by selective laser melting to consolidate the nanocomposites.
summary_en.result: The nanocomposites exhibited improved microhardness and wear resistance compared to pure H13 steel.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through microhardness measurements and dry sliding wear tests.
